name: Ramp
text: We should add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page that only appears when focused, allowing keyboard users to bypass navigation and jump to main content. This decision prioritizes keyboard navigation over potential visual clutter, accepting the trade-off that the link will not be visible to mouse users. By doing so, we ensure that users who rely on keyboard navigation can quickly access the main content, improving their overall experience. This approach aligns with the goal of making EXCAVA usable by everyone, particularly those with mobility impairments.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is that a high-contrast skip link still risks blending into the page when focused, defeating its purpose. A better alternative is a persistent skip link that’s always visible but subtly styled—no hover or focus tricks—so it’s reliably discoverable. Settle it by testing with keyboard users: if they can’t find it in under 3 seconds, the design fails.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **persistent, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, styled to always stand out against the background. This ensures keyboard users can reliably bypass navigation without relying on focus states that might fail or blend in. The trade-off is a small permanent element that some sighted users may notice, but it guarantees accessibility for everyone, including those with reduced contrast sensitivity or cognitive load issues.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a **bold, full-width skip bar** that appears only when keyboard-focused, with high contrast and no hover/focus tricks—tested with keyboard users to balance visibility and minimal intrusion. Owner: accessibility-w1.
